newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-SUNS SUSPEND HORRY TWO GAMES FOR THROWING TOWEL AT COACH.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-SUNS SUSPEND HORRY TWO GAMES FOR THROWING TOWEL AT COACH.

text.p: The Phoenix Suns suspended forward Robert Horry two games without pay Monday for throwing a towel in the face of coach Danny Ainge in Sunday night's game at Boston.

Midway through the fourth quarter of a 109-102 loss to the Celtics, Ainge substituted for Horry. The two sat next to each other and had words before Horry threw a towel in Ainge's face and walked to the end of the bench.
"Robert clearly crossed the line with regard to his deliberate actions toward Danny Ainge," said Suns general manager Bryan Colangelo.
"Players are entitled to display frustration, but there is a limit to what the staff will tolerate. Robert has apologised and discussed the issue at length with Danny."

Horry will miss the final two games of the club's five-game road trip, including Tuesday's game at Atlanta and Wednesday's contest at Washington. He will rejoin the team on Friday when the Suns take on the Charlotte Hornets in Phoenix.
Horry, a starter on Houston's back-to-back championship teams in 1994 and 1995, was one of four players traded by the Rockets to the Suns last August in exchange for All-Star forward Charles Barkley.
He has averaged 6.9 points and 3.7 rebounds in 32 games for Phoenix this season.
